newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:

* AMR's American Airlines made little progress on Thursday in its labour talks with the Allied Pilots Association, which has a history of disunity and has failed to drum up much support from other airline employees.
* The popularity of diet pills has prompted many companies in the $1.9 billion weight-loss industry to include them in their regimens, despite questions about the safety of the pills.
* The United States continues to threaten a rejection of a worldwide telecommunications pact, despite the fact that most other countries appear ready to make a deal.

* American General's $1.8 billion stock pact to acquire USLIFE, the largest of American General's five acquisitions over the last two years, creates a company that ranks among the top four life insurers in the country.
* Only 82 days after reaching the 6,000-point mark, the Dow industrials surged 60.81 points to close at 7,022.44.
* The yield on the 30-year bond fell to 6.62 percent from 6.71 percent.
* Retail sales rose modestly in January, and last week's initial claims for unemployment benefits fell.

* The Securities and Exchange Commission sued former Qualis Care LP chairman John Hall and an associate, accusing them of looting Towers Financial, the bankrupt company whose creditors they were supposed to help.
* The Federal Trade Commission may challenge Staples' $3.4 billion acquisition of Office Depot unless Staples can prove that the merger will not cause higher consumer prices.
* H.J. Heinz and Campbell Soup agreed to settle their dispute over Heinz's effort to hire Campbell executive Daniel O'Neill.
* British media company Pearson Plc said it might take a $163 million charge against last year's earnings because of accounting irregularities at its Penguin USA book publishing unit.
* South Korean prosecutors arrested a former cabinet minister and two parliament members accused of accepting bribes from the founder of Hanbo Steel Co.
* Philips Electronics reported a fourth-quarter net loss connected with charges for an overhaul and lower sales growth.
* Nokia said its pretax profit rose 76 percent in the fourth quarter and that it expected continued strong growth this year.

* A coalition of sporting goods makers pledged not to sell soccer balls made by children in Pakistan after a survey by the International Labour Organisation and others counted at least 14,700 children aged 14 years and under working full time stitching balls for less than the minimum wage.
